name: Chobham
description:
In days when the open practice of magic was forbidden, freethinking families sent their gifted offspring to a humble farmhouse deep in the woods where they could cultivate their craft in safety and obscurity.

Some of those students chose to stick around, building their own hideaways along tracks between the trees. As the settlement grew, the inevitable friends and hangers-on accumulated. Soon the forest tracks were paved with cobbles and lined with taverns and shops, and the edge of the forest was pushed back to make way for vineyards and orchards.

Other centers of learning have since overtaken Chobham in prominence, but it remains a destination for the young, the bohemian and those who'd like to feel young and bohemian for a day. There are those who say that the borders between our world and other worlds have been "worn thin" from the long years of arcane study and practice here, and you can hardly turn round without bumping into a fortune teller, soothsayer or impromptu seance.

Indeed, when the sun goes down, the ancient forest and its fecund darkness seems to reach toward the town, and in the morning seems a bit closer than perhaps it was the day before. Is the air here thick with magic because of the people who came here, or did the people come here because the air is thick with magic?

hooks.name: The Chokewood
hooks.description:
One of the old school's founders recently went missing on a trip into the forest. Search parties were rebuffed as, in a matter of days, strange, rapacious, fast-growing vines spread outward from the heart of the forest, blocking the way with tangled walls of surging growth.

The vines now thickly cover every inch of forest for miles around and a fetid smell issues forth from beneath their choking leaves. They now threaten to smother the orchards and outlying houses of the town, and some say they have seen them reach for the bodies of animals and passersby. People have begun calling the forest "The Chokewood."
hooks.gmNotes:
At the end of a lane stands a great, old farmhouse, which was the secret school of magic that began Chobham all those years ago. It has been added onto and expanded many times, making it a hulking collection of structures attached to the original house. Greenhouse additions predominate.

On approaching, Our Heroes should encounter some youths employed in keeping the vines back. They are maintaining a wide border between the edge of the forest and the gardens around the house by burning the vines with torches and small firebombs. They will readily demonstrate the danger of the vines by throwing a branch toward them, which the vines will of course snap forward to seize and break with terrifying force (and thus Our Heroes are acquainted with the eminent danger and also its fiery antidote).

In the house resides Auriga, a very ancient and very retired Elf who co-founded the school all those years ago with her husband Lemuel. Lemuel, being a bit younger, was wont to go wandering in the woods, bringing back new plants but also new spells - he found that he was much more able to "think magically" when walking in the woods. He of course is the one who went missing.

Auriga should offer Our Heroes various refreshments which grow improbably at her command (plates, cups and all) upon the various plants surrounding her easy chair in one of the greenhouses. She is friendly, forthcoming and frank. She clearly loves her husband but also knew that his wandering would bring trouble one way or another. Mostly she regrets the "brutish mess" of the vines, which strike her as "obviously magical" and "rather primitive in their execution." Despite her evident Transmutative powers, she doesn't get around very well anymore and thus has "no plans to go after that rascal" (meaning Lemuel).

Should Our Heroes offer their services, Auriga should outfit them with some helpful supplies - torches, plant knowledge, perhaps a spell scroll or two, whatever suits the party.

To begin with, there should be a combat with the vines themselves in order to gain entrance to the forest. Fire indeed keeps them at bay, but they should dart in and attempt to grab and squeeze an adventurer or two. Whoever is squeezed should experience a brief and vague magical sense of someone calling for help through the vines themselves.

Having passed the outer wall of vines, Our Heroes should find the forest intact but in a surprisingly advanced state of decay. Large, colorful and alien shapes - molds, fungi and other strange growths - abound and cover all surfaces, and spores are heavy in the air (consider some sort of periodic, recurring check to account for this).

Serve up as many encounters/conflicts as you care for as they wind their dark way through the ancient trees, but be sure to have one of these involve a dead creature or inanimate object made mobile and hostile by the fungi that permeate the forest. Perhaps upon inflicting a wound or defeating the foe, its innards are revealed to be shot through with multicolored mycelia, which twitch and pulse like muscle fibers. Touching these should deliver a brief and vague magical sense - similar to that of the vines, but in this case a sense of a calm, powerful presence that seems to beckon them toward the heart of the forest.

The darkness deepens as Our Heroes continue. Perhaps there is some attractive bioluminescence, literally or figuratively drawing them forward. Above and around them the vines are now aligned directionally, their tangled lines converging on a central point. Here of course is poor Lemuel, and here you may choose one of two ways:

OPTION 1: The calm, powerful, beckoning presence is that of the forest itself.
OPTION 2: The calm, powerful, beckoning presence is Auriga.

Whichever evil you choose, it has been luring people into its dark heart to feed on them for years beyond count. The method of "feeding" is up to you to determine, as well as the motivation behind it all (as it should be in accordance with the forces of your campaign world), but in any case the point is that Lemuel finally got wise to what was going on. In his moment of discovery, here at the heart of the forest, the evil force moved to take him and he had to act fast - hence the "brutish" nature of the vine growth spell he cast in desperation, which shielded him bodily (Our Heroes should find him fully wrapped and suspended in vines, completely exhausted), and which has choked off the forest's supply of sunlight.

If you chose Option 1, Our Heroes find Lemuel in, essentially, a standoff with the forest: it will rot and die if his vines persist, but (and here we learn a sad truth) it has managed to reach its mycelia into the house and into the plants around Auriga in her greenhouse. Thus, her life hangs in the balance.

If you chose Option 2, Our Heroes come to the grim realization that they were sent out here by a wife to kill her husband, and that she likely intends to kill - nay, eat - them as well if she can manage it.

In either case, Lemuel can offer passage back to the house via a ride on the vines if Our Heroes will attempt to (Option 1) wrest Auriga from the subterranean, multicolored clutches of the forest; or (Option 2) destroy his very evil wife.

The final conflict is, in either case, essentially the same: Our Heroes return to the house to face off against a myco-jacked Auriga (the difference being whether she or the mycelia are running the show) as well as a roomful of big, nasty, animate plants.

Bonus points for foreshadowing with tales in town of people going missing in the forest with some regularity, a wine cellar with mycelia incursions, etc. Further bonus points for giving the first interaction with Auriga a few notes of ominous strangeness in accordance with the flavor of evil you choose.

hooks.name: "Trout Boys Swim Upstream"
hooks.description: A gang of ruffians calling themselves The Trout Boys have been waylaying travelers and merchants on the river. They skew young in age and initially their takings were humble, but recently they have been hitting more ambitious targets and word is starting to spread that travel to and from Chobham is not safe.
hooks.gmNotes:
What started as a series of cruel pranks became much more serious when the Boys unwittingly targeted a barge of illicit goods, piloted by hardened gangsters from a larger city. Not only did the attack backfire, but the Trout Boys were forced into the fold of the larger crime organization, which immediately started demanding that they escalate their operations.

Many of the Trout Boys are local youths, who mix with the rest of the town by day. Maybe some of them are even from prominent families. Perhaps there is a discoverable tell by which to identify them: a fishhook tattoo, an unusual phrase, a hairstyle, etc.

Our Heroes should have no trouble disrupting some small-time, ill-conceived operation on the river. Caught in the act, the Boys' ire should quickly melt into fear: fear of being found out by their elders, but more so of the wrath of their bosses.

This latter fear will prove to be well-founded, though the wrath will be directed at Our Heroes. In messing with the Trout Boys, they have messed with the larger organization, which wants to defend its newly-won territory. A disproportionate show of force should follow, perhaps catching Our Heroes unawares at night in their lodgings, leading to a close-quarters fight with a ludicrous number of goons.

Perhaps that's as far as this goes, but if you like, you could widen the scale of the attack to threaten the entire town: houses and orchards are set to flame, arcane academics running in the street in their nightshirts, etc. Maybe the head of the crime syndicate knows a thing or two about the arcane arts and wants to get their hands on something powerful that's rumored to be in Chobham?

hooks.name: Ill Fortune
hooks.description: Two prominent fortune-tellers had a row recently and began publicly proclaiming ill-fortunes for one another. The problem is that the predictions keep coming true. At first they were inconveniences and minor setbacks - stolen shoes, upset stomach - but in recent days a house fire, a head injury and a haunting have all come to pass after being predicted the day before. It's unclear if the bad blood is breeding bad luck, or if these soothsayers are actually willing these events into reality.
hooks.gmNotes:
The meat of the nut here is that each of the fortune-tellers is connected to a deity, those deities are themselves engaged in their own cosmic row, and the fortune-tellers have the misfortune of being the pawns in a cruel proxy battle.

The identities and natures of the deities are up to you (consider a pair with opposite domains, like night and day), as well as to what degree the fortune-tellers are aware of their discipleship to these entities.

Moral ambiguity should be the goal here: there's no good or evil. The signs of the divine nature of the conflict should be come increasingly apparent as the fortunes told become more dire and threaten more and more of the town, culminating in an actual manifestation of the deities and whatever retinue you care to give each of them for a battle in the streets, fields and orchards of Chobham.

Can Our Heroes make peace and save the town from destruction?
